scenes.say: Nobody is watching you as much as you think. Not even close.
The spotlight effect: you're the centre of your story, so you assume you're the centre of everyone's.
Gilovich and colleagues had students walk into a room in an embarrassing T-shirt.
scenes.note: Source: Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky (2000), JPSP · rounded

scenes.say: They guessed about half the room noticed. In reality, about {real}.
Everyone else is too busy worrying about their own spotlight.
What stops you trying new things usually isn't other people's eyes. It's the ones you imagine.

takeaway: What stops you trying new things usually isn't other people's eyes. It's the ones you imagine.
